a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is furosemide; the closest supplied measured context is bumetanide, which shares the sulfamoylbenzoic acid diuretic core and has measured human absolute oral bioavailability of 0.66–0.86 (66–86%) across multiple studies, with L2 records describing 80–100% and near-complete oral bioavailability.

All other supplied measured oral-bioavailability contexts are above the 20% threshold: PAS 50–60%, probenecid ~100%, diclofenac ~50%, bromfenac 67%, safinamide 95%, amlodipine 58%, rigosertib 35%, PF-05241328 38%, and telmisartan 42%.

L6 hepatic-clearance records for azosemide, the closest structural analog (tetrazole replaces the carboxyl and thienylmethyl replaces furfuryl), show low rat hepatic microsomal intrinsic clearance (2.70 and 4.51 ×10^-3 ml/min) and substantial unchanged parent in S9; bumetanide shows no CYP2E1-mediated clearance. This is mechanistic evidence against a large hepatic first-pass loss, though not a direct F measurement.
